title: Streaming gateway errors show reason phrase instead of upstream message for non-OpenAI bodies
answers: streaming AI gateway request returns 400 Bad Request with no provider explanation
Bedrock error message missing from streamed gateway response
why does stream error only say 'Bad Request' while non-streaming shows the real error
upstream error detail dropped in send_stream_request
body:
Symptom: A streaming request through the AI Gateway fails with only the HTTP reason phrase (e.g. "400: Bad Request") while the same request sent non-streaming shows the provider's explanation. Seen with Amazon Bedrock, whose error body is top-level {"message": ...}.
Root cause: mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py:send_stream_request read only error_body.get("error", {}).get("message", e.message), so any non-OpenAI-shaped body fell back to aiohttp's reason phrase, and a non-JSON body was discarded.
Fix pattern: Extract the detail through the shared mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py:_error_detail (error.message, then top-level message, then the whole body), and chain fallbacks json -> response.text() -> e.message. Keep the same chain in send_proxy_request.
Constraints: send_request is intentionally unchanged; it already returns the whole body and changing it alters the response shape non-streaming callers see.
applies: Error handling of upstream HTTP responses in mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py; applies to any provider helper that surfaces upstream error bodies to users.
says: Streaming model requests fail with generic bad request messages instead of provider explanations.
Streamed Bedrock completion returns four hundred without showing why the request was rejected.
Show the actual upstream provider error message when streaming model generation fails.
Why does non-streaming show provider error details while streaming only displays bad request?
Display provider rejection reasons in streaming gateway responses instead of generic status phrases.
search: Upstream HTTP error handling in mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py must extract response details using mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py:_error_detail across streaming and proxy requests. In send_stream_request, expecting OpenAI-formatted error payloads dropped upstream messages from providers like Amazon Bedrock that return a top-level message field or non-JSON payloads, collapsing errors to generic HTTP reason phrases. The helper extracts error.message, then top-level message, then the entire body, chaining fallbacks from JSON to response.text() and e.message in send_stream_request and send_proxy_request. send_request remains intentionally unchanged because it already returns the entire response body and altering it would change the response format seen by non-streaming callers.
